clue.text: Follower died here throttled by soldier?

indicators.note: something throttled is squeezed with hands closed around it, so these words sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker caste of ant
D is the standard abbreviation for died
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim scene: someone's devoted follower died on this spot, strangled by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is an insect, not a military man: soldier ants are the large-jawed caste that defends the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or disciple, so the word is a straightforward synonym for a follower.

clue.text: Dangerous substance: put a distress call around first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the distress call is placed so that it goes round the word that comes after, enclosing it

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
first place is the best

explanation.surface: A warning that a hazardous material has been found, so a distress call should be put out first.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral whose dust causes lung disease, a classic example of a hazardous material.

clue.text: Roll a constant husband leaves to be eaten

parts.note: to roll or turn over is to spin
taken as written
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: It reads as if a husband walks out on a roll, with the 'leaves' being a departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the verb of the departing husband, but it is a noun: the green leaves of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy vegetable, eaten as cooked or raw leaves, so it is an example of edible foliage.

clue.text: Spanish force a Frenchman to enter Rada

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so the Frenchman goes inside the drama school's name

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is joining RADA, the London drama school, as if part of an invading force.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school; M goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armada was the Spanish fleet sent against England in 1588, and the word means a naval force.

clue.text: Peacekeepers take break, causing disquiet

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
a break is a rest

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops go off duty, and trouble breaks out while they are resting.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is public disturbance or agitation, a synonym for disquiet in the sense of a troubled state.

clue.text: Spy boss diverted up sideroad on way to work

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: traffic that is diverted is sent along a different route, so the following letters take a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spymaster is rerouted up a side road on the commute to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way to work' looks like a commute, but it means a method of working. M is the spy chief in the Bond books.
explanation.definitionFit: Modus operandi is Latin for a method of operating, a person's characteristic procedure for getting things done.

clue.text: Old woman and son, cleric, manage badly

parts.note: an old woman is slang for one's mother, ma
a son is a lad
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A mother, her son and a churchman together make a mess of running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is informal for mother, giving MA.
explanation.definitionFit: To maladminister is to run an organisation or affairs inefficiently or dishonestly, a synonym for mismanaging.

clue.text: Double success after Latin edict redrafted

indicators.note: one piece placed after another means the first-named piece comes second in the answer
a redrafted document has its wording reworked, so these letters are set down in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a win is a success

explanation.surface: Someone scores a triumph after rewriting an old decree in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a person who looks exactly like another, and an identical twin is the clearest example of such a lookalike.

clue.text: Thermal garment to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a warm jacket made of soft synthetic pile
second meaning: to swindle someone out of their money

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like laundry instructions for a warm jacket, but 'take to the cleaners' is the idiom for cheating someone of their money.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a warm synthetic top, and to fleece someone is to overcharge or swindle them, the same as taking them to the cleaners.

clue.text: A number want sandwiches trimmed

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so the verb puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to want something is to need it
taken as written
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Several people are hungry for sandwiches with the crusts cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food the people want, but it is a verb meaning to hold between two outer layers.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to make tidy, so neatened means tidied up, which is what trimmed means of a hedge or a beard.

clue.text: For starters see physio attending health resort

indicators.note: starters are what come at the beginning of a meal, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: At a health resort, the first thing you do is see the physiotherapist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a place with mineral springs or treatments that people visit to improve their health.

clue.text: Dawn and Victor trapped in a hollow

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something trapped in a place is held inside it, so the letter for Victor goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two people named Dawn and Victor are stuck together in a hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn reads as a woman's name beside Victor, but it is the definition, meaning a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means the arrival or beginning of something, which matches dawn in the figurative sense of a start.

clue.text: Abstinence? Charlie hurried to embrace it!

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so the word for hurried goes round the following one

parts.note: hasty means done in a hurry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A joke at Charlie's expense: so much for abstaining, he rushed to embrace it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastity is abstaining from sexual relations, so it is a specific kind of abstinence.

clue.text: Long blade hidden by this killer

indicators.note: something hidden by the following words is concealed in their letters, running across the word break

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A murderer has concealed a long knife.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'long blade' sounds like a weapon in a murder story, but it is something you strap to your boot on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed to a boot, and is often called a blade in the sense of a flat strip.

clue.text: Agree examination for Darwin's survivors?

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective used as a noun, 'the fittest'

parts.note: to fit is to agree or match, as a description fits the facts
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Someone is agreeing to sit an exam on evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Survival of the fittest' is the phrase summarising Darwin's theory of natural selection; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Under natural selection those best adapted to their environment live on, so the survivors in the phrase are the best adapted ones.

clue.text: She reigned over us a very long time

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen who reigned over Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribute to the late Queen, who reigned over the nation for a remarkably long time.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth; in this down answer her initials sit above A.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long, distinct period of history, so it fits a very long stretch of time.

clue.text: Anguished expression from serious expert

parts.note: grim means stern and serious
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A solemn specialist pulls a pained face.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look showing pain or disgust, so it is an anguished expression.

clue.text: Think again about high seas engulfing ship

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the letters for ship end up surrounded
someone high is intoxicated and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor reconsiders whether to sail, with huge waves swamping a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High seas' looks like a fixed phrase for open ocean, but 'high' is the signal to jumble the letters of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate again, which is to reconsider or think something over a second time.

clue.text: Snowball in face — fell over!

parts.note: mush is British slang for the face

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so in this down entry the word for fell is read upwards

parts.note: a fell is an upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone takes a snowball in the face and falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snowball' and 'fell' both pretend to be about a winter accident; snowball is a verb meaning grow fast, and a fell is a northern English hill moor.
explanation.definitionFit: To snowball is to grow rapidly and cumulatively, which is exactly what to mushroom means as a verb.

clue.text: Hospital worker certainly not disorganised

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hospital attendant who does non-medical tasks
second meaning: neat and well arranged

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a tidy hospital employee; the two halves are separate meanings, one a noun and one an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly is a hospital attendant, and as an adjective the word means methodical and tidy, the opposite of chaotic.

clue.text: Endlessly detestable beer for Hamlet character

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the word for detestable loses its final letter

parts.note: vile means detestable
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An actor playing a role in Hamlet complains about terrible beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's play, but here it is a small settlement, so its character is someone who lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village, so a person living there is a villager, its resident.

clue.text: Raised in family like some wild animal

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the raised piece is placed within the word for family

parts.note: a family line is a lineage
raised means up

explanation.surface: Someone brought up in a household that behaves like wild beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised in family' reads as upbringing; it is really an instruction to place one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine means relating to or resembling wolves, and the wolf is a wild animal.

clue.text: Revolutionary Indian instrument good for nothing

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the instrument's name is read backwards

parts.note: the sitar is a long-necked Indian lute

explanation.surface: A rebellious sitar is dismissed as useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good for nothing' reads as one phrase meaning worthless; split it, and good gives G while 'for nothing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, given without payment, which is what getting something for nothing means.

clue.text: Italian monk in Le Mans sloshed

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, and a drunk's words come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian monk gets drunk at the Le Mans motor race in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Anselm was a Benedictine monk born in Aosta, Italy, who became Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Cut record for underworld figure

indicators.note: a cut word is trimmed short, so the following word loses its last letter

parts.note: a disc is a record

explanation.surface: A gangster cuts a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld figure' suggests a gangster, but it is the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman ruler of the land of the dead, the counterpart of Pluto or Hades.

clue.text: Loads backing call for industrial action

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for loads is read from right to left

parts.note: pots of money means loads of it
to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager

explanation.surface: Many workers support a call for a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt to work by employees as a protest, which is a form of strike action.

clue.text: Stretch in lake twists to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry going west is going right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
to warp is to twist out of shape

explanation.surface: A stretch of a lake winds westward.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to spread out the limbs, or to spread out over an area, much as one stretches.

clue.text: Couples with RNIB worked on pickle-fork

indicators.note: something worked is kneaded or shaped by hand, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the Royal National Institute of Blind People, a UK charity, used for its letters
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pairs of volunteers help the RNIB, a British charity for blind people, to make a pickle fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked on' looks like one phrase, but only 'worked' is the signal; 'on' joins COUPLES and RNIB in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's nonsense word came to name a three-pronged fork with a cutting edge, used for pickles or hors d'oeuvres.
